The weight of a mode is a sum over the samples of the chain, each sample with the width of
its own step,
\begin{equation}
\lambda_m \simeq \sigma \sum_{k=0}^{W} [w_k \, \mathrm{sinc}(\pi k/W)] \, g(w_k) \, \Delta w .
\end{equation}
The likelihood of the first state is an integral over the later states of a product of the
steps of the chain,
\[ p(x_0) = \int \prod_{t=1}^{T} p_t(x_{t-1} \mid x_t) \, dx_{1:T} . \]
Each step has a mean and a spread of its own.

\newpage

% A few points lower than the left column, so that the numbered line here is level with the
% sum on the left and with the limit under it.
\vspace*{5pt}
The cross entropy of two distributions over the same outcomes is a sum over the outcomes
of the chain,
\begin{equation}
C(p, q) = - \sum_{i=1}^{W} p_i \log q_i .
\end{equation}
It is zero only when the two distributions are the same.

\noindent The energy of a chain:
\[ E_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} e_i + E_{\mathrm{reg}} \]
